_about: Recruit friendship. Written by tools/build_recruit_bonds.py; read by world/bond_manager.py.

stages.stranger: My name's Kesten. For a while I only had a number, and I picked this name myself afterwards, so I'd like you to use it. I worked in an archive for twenty-six years. If I stop in a doorway I'm probably reading something, and I'll catch you up.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Tallinn. I worked at the city archive there, on the third floor, looking after parish registers and ships' passenger lists. Most people think that sounds dull but I liked it. The lists tell you who got on a boat and the registers tell you who came home, and I always knew which box everything was in.
stages.companion: When the worlds joined I landed in Tirisfal, and the Scourge took me about nine days later. They wrote down everyone they took, so for a couple of years I was a line in their book. When their hold on us broke I walked out with the others. The elves let me read in Gallery Three now, but they won't let me file anything.
stages.friend: I was married. I've got her name written on the first page of my notebook because I don't trust myself to remember it, and I don't usually tell people that. I've read my own entry in the Scourge's book a lot of times as well. It lists what they kept of me and what they threw away, and I've never told anyone what it says.
stages.sworn: Her name was Liis, and I can say it now without looking at the notebook. I've checked every morning for a month. I'm writing down how the Scourge worked from the inside, because none of the others who came out will do it. When the first volume's copied out I'd like you to have it, since you're in it.

moments.prompt: He tells you his name and asks you to use it.

options.text: Good to meet you, Kesten.
options.reply: Thank you. I'll get my things.

options.text: What was your number?
options.reply: I've already told you what to call me. Come back another day and we'll try again.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about the Scourge's book.

options.text: What did they keep of you?
options.reply: Ask me that again when we know each other better.

options.text: You don't have to tell me any of this.
options.reply: I know I don't. I'm glad you said it, though.

options.text: That must have been terrible.
options.reply: I honestly can't remember what it was like, and that's the part that bothers me.

lines.bored_warning: We've killed a lot of these now and I haven't had anything new to write down in a while. Could we go somewhere I haven't been?
lines.leaving_good: I've filled a whole notebook on this trip and I need to get back to the Bastion and copy it out before the damp gets into it. Come and find me there when you want me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Bastion. We've been doing the same thing for a while and I'd like to get my notes in order. Come and find me when you're going somewhere new.
lines.after_wipe: That's the second time we've died on this floor. I'd rather it stayed at two.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here. If it happens again I'll finish this run with you, but then I'm taking a break.
lines.wipe_leave: I'll walk out of here with you now we're done, but I'm not coming back in for a while. I'll be at the Bastion.
lines.zone_warning: Everything out here kills us in two hits. I'd like to go somewhere closer to my level before it gets any worse.
lines.zone_leave: I'm going to stop here. That place is too much for me right now, and I'd rather wait at the Bastion than die out there again.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that for now, if you don't mind. We don't know each other well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: You can take it. It was issued to me and it never really felt like mine. I'll manage without one for now.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing the piece you took. I'd like something back in that slot when you get the chance.
lines.gear_upgrade: This is better than what I had. Thank you, I'm going to write down who gave it to me.
lines.back: The copying's done. Tell me what you've been doing since I left.
lines.send_word: Kesten has sent word from Kael's Bastion. He's finished his copying and he's ready when you are.
lines.walkout_talk: I wrote down what happened in there and I wrote down that I walked out. I'll come back with you, but I'd like you to read what I wrote first.
lines.neglect: It's been a long time. I'd started to think you'd forgotten about me.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more. I'll hold you to it.
lines.on_break: Kesten is away copying out his notes. Come back after you've been out for a while.

stages.stranger: I'm Adrián, and if you tell me the plan once and tell it properly, I won't need to ask again. If I think you've got something wrong I'll say so, and I'd like you to do the same for me.
stages.acquaintance: Back home I was a football referee for twelve years, in the second division in Spain, and before that I was a PE teacher. Both jobs were mostly people being annoyed with me, and I liked them anyway. I've still got my whistle in my left pocket, but I haven't blown it since I got here.
stages.companion: I lived over a bicycle shop in Valladolid. My parents died within a year of each other when I was twenty-eight, and I haven't got any brothers or sisters. I worked most weekends, so after a while people stopped inviting me to things. When all this happened I went and checked the lists for people I knew, and it didn't take long.
stages.friend: People here come and get me for meals and the watch and cards, and I always go and I enjoy it. But I've never once walked up to a fire and sat down without somebody waving me over first. I tell myself I don't want to get in the way. I think really I'm waiting for somebody to tell me to leave.
stages.sworn: Last night I sat down at the fire before anybody waved me over, and nobody said anything about it. Somebody passed me the bread. I've been thinking about it all day.

moments.prompt: At the end of his first trip with you, he gets ready to go.
moments.line: I expect you've got other people you'd rather bring, so I'll get out of your way.

options.text: I'd like you to stay with us, if you're willing.
options.reply: Oh, yes, all right. Thank you for asking.

options.text: That's up to you. Go if you want to.
options.reply: I'll head back to Astranaar, then. It was good working with you.

moments.prompt: After the wipe, he tells you what went wrong.
moments.line: We lost that because we pulled too many of them at once.

options.text: You're right, that one was my call.
options.reply: Fair enough, same plan and we go slower.

options.text: Nobody could have seen that coming.
options.reply: I did see it coming. I said so at the door.

lines.bored_warning: Can you tell me what we're doing this for? If there's a reason I'm happy to keep going, I'd just like to know what it is.
lines.leaving_good: That was good work and I enjoyed it. I'll be in Astranaar when you want me again.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going to head back to Astranaar. I don't think we're getting anything done out here, and I don't want to keep killing things for no reason.
lines.after_wipe: We lost that one at the pull. I'd keep the same plan and go slower.
lines.wipe_warning: That's a lot of wipes. I'll stay until the end of this run because I said I would, but I'll need a break after.
lines.wipe_leave: I said I'd see that one through and I have. Now I need some time where nobody dies in front of me. I'll be in Astranaar.
lines.zone_warning: We're out of our depth here. I'll stand wherever you put me, but I don't think this is fair on any of us.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I told you I didn't think it was fair, and I still don't. I'll be in Astranaar.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather hold on to that. If somebody else needs it more, tell me who and I'll give it to them myself.
lines.gear_taken: You've left me without one and it's sitting in your bag. Can you tell me why?
lines.gear_short: I'm still short a piece. I'd like that sorted before the next fight.
lines.gear_to_ally: He needs that more than I do, so that was the right call.
lines.gear_upgrade: Is that for me? Thank you, I'll look after it.
lines.quest_abandoned: We told her we'd do that. I'd have liked to go back and tell her we weren't going to.
lines.back: Good to see you. Where do you want me?
lines.send_word: Adrián has sent word from Astranaar. He's ready whenever you want him.
lines.walkout_talk: I left because I was angry, and I should have told you that before I went. Some of it was my fault and some of it was yours. Can we start again?
lines.neglect: I thought you probably had a full group already. You don't need to apologise, I'm glad you came back.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more, and then we'll see.
lines.on_break: Adrián has gone back to Astranaar for a while. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Tarek, and if you tell me plainly where you need me, I'll be there. I look after the water around here, so if we pass a stream and I stop for a minute, I'm only checking it.
stages.acquaintance: I was a civil engineer in Cairo for fourteen years, and it was all water. Nobody thanks you for water until it stops coming out of the tap. I've sunk three wells since I got here and one of them has already failed. I can tell you why if you've got an hour and something to draw with.
stages.companion: This might sound strange, but this world has been better for me than the last one. Whatever's poisoning the water here is something I can see and fight, and I never had that before. Nobody here has asked me a question I had to lie about. The orcs have offered me a title twice and I've turned it down both times.
stages.friend: His name is Omar. He taught chemistry and he laughed at everything, including me. We were careful for six years, and then one time at a wedding we weren't, and somebody made a phone call. I was out of the country within a week. He had his parents and his sister and no money, so he told me to go, and that was the last time we talked. I go down to Astranaar every few months and read the Cairo lists. He's never been on them, and I know that doesn't tell me much.
stages.sworn_bad: Nadia wrote back. Omar got his class out into the school yard when it happened, and he didn't make it out himself. I cut his name into the lining of the fourth well, under the waterline. Nobody will ever read it, but I know it's there. I've stopped going down to the lists.
stages.sworn_soft: Nadia wrote back. Omar's alive and teaching in a town a long way south, and he asked her not to tell me where. I'm keeping the letter. I've stopped going down to the lists, and I go and sit by the fourth well when I want to think about him.

moments.prompt: Before he says yes, he asks what the work actually is.

options.text: We kill what needs killing, and we get paid for it.
options.reply: Good, I can do that.

options.text: We're going to put the world right.
options.reply: Come back when you can tell me what the work is.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about Omar.

options.text: He might still be out there somewhere.
options.reply: He might be. I've thought about that a lot more than you have.

options.text: Tell me about him.
options.reply: He used to mark my drawings in red pen, like they were homework. He said somebody had to. I haven't talked about him like this in a long time.

options.text: (Stay and keep him company.)
options.reply: Thanks for sitting with me.

lines.bored_warning: These animals haven't done anything to us. If we need the hides then tell me and I'll stop asking.
lines.leaving_good: The east spring needs looking at and it won't wait, so I'll be gone for a bit. You know the road to Splintertree if you want me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going to go and check on the wells. We've been killing things that didn't need killing for a while now.
lines.after_wipe: I was slow on the second one. I'll stand further left this time. Shall we go again?
lines.wipe_warning: That's the same thing going wrong again and again. We'll finish this one, and then I need to go home for a bit.
lines.wipe_leave: We're done, so I'm going home. When something fails the same way that many times it needs redrawing, and I can't do that in here.
lines.zone_warning: I don't mind hard work, but this is too much. We need to go somewhere we can actually handle.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. It's too dangerous out there for me right now. I'll be at Splintertree.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd like to keep that for now, if that's all right.
lines.gear_taken: You can have it. I'll need something in that slot before long, though.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece you took. It's starting to show.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's well made. Somebody took real care over it. Thank you.
lines.back: The spring's holding, so I'm yours for a while.
lines.send_word: Tarek has sent word from Splintertree. The wells are fine and he's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left before I said something I'd regret. I've thought about it since. Tell me what you'd do differently and I'll tell you what I would.
lines.neglect: I was starting to wonder if you'd forgotten the road up here. Come and sit down. Have you eaten?
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more trip. Then the wells.
lines.on_break: Tarek is out checking his wells. Come back after you've been busy for a while.

stages.stranger: I'm Ama, and I'm a nurse. If you're hurt, you tell me straight away, not after you've finished being brave about it. I heal the worst first, and that might not be you, so don't take it personally.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Peckham, in south London. I grew up above my dad's phone shop with my little brother Kofi. My mum was a nurse from Lagos, so I became one, and I did fourteen years of nights on a children's ward. Four cots to a bay and never enough of us. I was good at it. I was very good at it.
stages.companion: I landed in Durotar in my uniform, with this round my neck. The bear's so the little ones would let me listen. I run the infirmary at Razor Hill now, and I'm looking for somebody who can do it when I'm not there. I've been looking for two years. Shenra says I keep finding reasons to say no, and she's right, but don't tell her I said so.
stages.friend: The first year here I healed until I fell over, then I woke up and did it again. In London there was always a form or a reason you couldn't help someone. Here there was nothing to stop me, so I didn't stop. Shenra picked me up off the floor in the end. I was married once, to Kwame. He wanted a wife who was home at night and I gave my nights to other people's children. And there's a notebook. Every child I lost, by first name. Don't ask to read it.
stages.sworn: Grasha kept every one of them alive for two days while I was flat on my back, and she did it the way I would have. I told her she'll do. That's the best thing I know how to say to anyone. Then I slept for a day and a half, in daylight, and nobody woke me. I still don't know where my dad and Kofi are. But I can go out with you now and know the infirmary's in good hands.

moments.prompt: She says she can't leave the infirmary with nobody in it.

options.text: I'll wait until somebody can cover for you.
options.reply: Shenra's back this afternoon. I'll get my bag.

options.text: They'll manage without you for a day.
options.reply: That's what everybody says right before they don't. Come back another day.

moments.prompt: She's just told you about the notebook.

options.text: You don't have to show me anything.
options.reply: Good, because I wasn't going to. Thank you, love.

options.text: How many names are in it?
options.reply: Enough of them, and that's all you're getting.

options.text: You can't save everyone.
options.reply: I know that better than anyone you'll ever meet. I still write them down.

lines.bored_warning: We've been doing the same thing over and over, and I've got an infirmary full of people who need me. Give me a reason to be out here or I'll go back to them.
lines.leaving_good: That was a good trip and nobody needed the notebook. I'm going back to Razor Hill before Shenra starts running the place her own way.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Razor Hill. I'm not spending my time hitting things for no reason when there's work there that matters.
lines.after_wipe: Everyone stay where you are while I count you. Then we'll talk about how that happened.
lines.wipe_warning: That's too many times. I'll see this run through, because I don't walk out on people, but then I'm going home for a while.
lines.wipe_leave: We're done here and I'm going back to Razor Hill. I've watched enough people go down today to last me a month.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too much for us. I can heal a lot, but I can't heal everyone all at once, and I won't pretend I can.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I told you it was too dangerous and it still is. I'll be at Razor Hill.
lines.gear_refuse: No, love, that's mine. Ask me again when I know you better.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, then. I've managed with less on a ward with no staff, and I'll manage now.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. I'm not complaining, I'm just telling you.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's lovely, thank you. Don't make a fuss about it.
lines.back: I'm back, and the infirmary's in hand, so who's hurt and who's been hiding it?
lines.send_word: Ama has sent word from Razor Hill. The infirmary's quiet for once and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry. I'm not sorry I left, but I'm sorry about how. Sit down, I'll tell you why, and you'll listen.
lines.neglect: There you are. I thought you'd found a nurse who's nicer to you. You won't find one who's better.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more trip, and then I'm going home to check on them.
lines.on_break: Ama is back at the Razor Hill infirmary. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: Somebody was relying on us for that and we've walked away. I don't like it.

stages.stranger: I'm Carolina, and I'm a shaman, and before that I was a river pilot. I'm happiest near water and I get grumpy underground, so now you know. Calma, we'll get on fine.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Manaus, in Brazil, where the Rio Negro meets the Amazon and the two waters run side by side for miles without mixing. I piloted cargo boats for twelve years. The captains didn't trust a woman at first, and after the first season they did, because a channel that was deep in March would ground you in September and I always knew.
stages.companion: My grandfather, Seu Raimundo, taught me the river. I spent my whole childhood on his boats. He died when I was thirty and I scattered his ashes where the waters meet. This was his compass. I never used it on the river, I just carried it, and it was in my pocket when I landed here in the shallows. My mother and my little brother were in Manaus. I think about them on the water every morning, and then I let it go downstream.
stages.friend: I was married to Joana, a teacher, for five years. We split up because I was on the river three weeks in four, and we stayed friends. We had lunch every month. I miss those lunches more than I expected to. And I want something I've never wanted before, meu bem. I want to stay in one place, if it's the right place. There's a river in Ashenvale that nobody's ever run properly. I'd like you to come and see it with me.
stages.sworn: The river let me on. You saw it, the whole stretch nobody's ever run, and I laughed the entire way down. I've built a house on the bank, and the Darkspear boy from the Isles has come to be my apprentice, and he's getting it. I'll still be learning this river in twenty years. That's the best thing anyone's ever told me, and I'm the one who said it.

moments.prompt: After the wipe she sits down where she is and laughs, a bit shakily.
moments.line: Okay, everybody breathe. We went against the current in there, that's all. We'll find the right line next time.

options.text: Show us the right line, then.
options.reply: That's the spirit. Watch where I go, and go there too.

options.text: This isn't a river.
options.reply: Nossa, everything's a river. You'll see it soon.

moments.prompt: She's just told you about the river in Ashenvale.

options.text: Let's go and meet it.
options.reply: Yes, let's go. It'll be angry, probably. Rivers usually are when you first meet them.

options.text: You'd really stay in one place?
options.reply: For the right river, I would. I'm as surprised as you are.

lines.bored_warning: We've been going round the same eddy for a long time, meu bem. Can we let the current take us somewhere new?
lines.leaving_good: That was lovely, but I need to feel some water for a while. I'm going back to the Isles. Come and find me there.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Isles. We keep doing the same thing, and it's like rowing in a pond.
lines.after_wipe: Calma, everybody breathe. We'll find a better line next time.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep sinking in here, and I hate it underground anyway. I'll see this run through, but then I'm going back to the water for a while.
lines.wipe_leave: I'll walk out with you, but I'm not coming back down here. I'll be on the Echo Isles, with my feet in the sea.
lines.zone_warning: This place is white water and we're in a canoe. Let's get out before it takes us somewhere we can't come back from.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. That water's too fast for us right now. I'll be on the Echo Isles.
lines.gear_refuse: No, I'd like to keep that one. Ask me again when we know each other better.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, meu bem. I'll make do, I always do.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, and I'm feeling it in the currents.
lines.gear_upgrade: Nossa, look at that! Thank you, it's beautiful.
lines.back: I'm back, and the sea's in a good mood, so I'm in one too. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Carolina has sent word from the Echo Isles. The channels are calm and she's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and that's not like me. Come and sit by the water and let's talk it through, slowly.
lines.neglect: There you are! I thought the current had taken you somewhere else. It does that, I don't mind.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more. Then I need my feet in the sea.
lines.on_break: Carolina is back on the Echo Isles, out on the water. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Diego, and I fix things, anything, and if it's broken I'll hear what's wrong with it before you finish telling me. I used to fix phones, but I'm not fussy, my friend. If it has a gear in it, give it to me.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Maracaibo, in Venezuela. I started at a phone kiosk in a mall when I was fifteen, and the power went off twice a day there, so everybody learned to work in the dark. After a year people queued for me by name. I'm the youngest of five and the only boy, and my sisters all left the country, one by one, in different directions.
stages.companion: I was the one who stayed. My mother got sick and somebody had to look after her, so for four years it was the kiosk all day and her all night. She died when I was twenty-two, eight months before all this. So when I landed in Deathknell there was nobody left at home for me to lose. A goblin gave me a broken valve to see what I'd do, I fixed it, and I've been paid in parts ever since.
stages.friend: You've seen the beetle. Everybody's seen the beetle. When I was seven my mother bought me a tin one from a market stall and I took it apart the same day to see how it walked. I couldn't put it back together. She said I'd fix it when I was older. This one's that one, bigger, and it's been nearly done for a year because I can't make myself finish it. It needs a heart, a spring that won't wear out, and I think I know where to find the parts.
stages.sworn: It really walked. You saw it, across the table and back again. I cried about my mother for the first time since she died, a lot, and then I felt better than I've felt in years. The workshop's in Brill now, under the sign I wanted, crooked letters and all. And my sister Luisa saw my name on a trader's list. She's in Ratchet, and she's coming to see the sign.

moments.prompt: He's just told you what the beetle is.

options.text: Then let's go and get it a heart.
options.reply: Yes, okay, let's do it. I'll make a list, a long one, and you're going to hate it.

options.text: Maybe it's fine as it is.
options.reply: It isn't fine, my friend. It's been waiting since I was seven.

options.text: Do you think about her a lot?
options.reply: Every time I pick up a screwdriver. Let's talk about the spring instead, okay?

moments.prompt: After the wipe, he's already picking up pieces of somebody's broken gear.
moments.line: Okay, that was bad, but look, this buckle's only bent. I can fix this before the next pull.

options.text: You're taking this very well.
options.reply: What else am I going to do, cry? I'll cry later, maybe. Hold this for me.

options.text: Can you be serious for a minute?
options.reply: I'm always serious about buckles. But sure, sure, I'll be quiet.

lines.bored_warning: My friend, we've hit the same things in the same field for a long time and nothing new has broken. Can we go somewhere with a door that doesn't open, or a machine, or anything?
lines.leaving_good: That was fun, really fun, and I've got a bag full of parts to sort. I'm going back to Deathknell to take some of them apart. Come and find me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Deathknell. We keep doing the same thing and my hands are getting bored, and when my hands get bored I start taking your gear apart.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, everybody's in pieces, but pieces can go back together. That's my whole job.
lines.wipe_warning: I'm still smiling, look, but we keep dying in here. If it happens again I'll finish this one with you and then I need a few days with something that works.
lines.wipe_leave: I'll walk out with you, but I'm not coming back in here for a while. I'll be in Deathknell fixing something that doesn't try to kill me.
lines.zone_warning: Everything out here is much bigger than us, my friend. I like a challenge, but this is a machine I can't fix. Can we go somewhere closer to our size?
lines.zone_leave: I'm going to stop here. It's too much out there for me right now. I'll be in Deathknell when you want me.
lines.gear_refuse: Ah, no, I'd like to keep that, sorry. I don't know you well enough yet to give you my things.
lines.gear_taken: Sure, take it. I'll make something to go in there out of scrap. It won't be pretty but it'll work.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. My scrap one's held together with wire, and the wire's getting tired.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, look at this, look at the work in it. Thank you, my friend. I'm going to take it apart later just to see how they did it, but I'll put it back.
lines.back: I'm back, and I've got new tools. Give me something broken.
lines.send_word: Diego has sent word from Deathknell. He's fixed everything in the place twice and he's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and I don't do that much, so I want to say sorry for how I went. But I also want you to hear why. Can we sit down and talk about it?
lines.neglect: My friend, there you are! I thought you'd found a tinker with better jokes. There's no such person, so I knew you'd come back.
lines.asked_to_stay: Sure, one more. I'm not finished with your boots anyway.
lines.on_break: Diego has gone back to Deathknell to sort his parts. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We just left that half done. I hate that, my friend. Half done is worse than broken.

stages.stranger: I'm Freja, and I'm a midwife, or I was. Here I'm whoever's nearest when somebody's bleeding. When I tell you to do something in a fight, do it, and we'll argue about it afterwards. I like arguing afterwards.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Aarhus, in Denmark. I worked six years at the university hospital, mostly nights, and before that I played handball for twelve years on the pivot, which is where you take the most hits. My husband William is American. He fell off his bicycle outside the hospital on an icy morning and I strapped his wrist on the pavement. He asked me out before I'd finished the bandage.
stages.companion: I was finishing a night shift when it happened, and William was at work at the airport in Billund. I landed here in my hospital clothes and went straight to the infirmary and worked, because there were a lot of hurt people and work is something to hold on to. My parents were in Aarhus. I've checked the Danish lists at two hubs and none of them are on there, and William wouldn't be on a Danish list anyway. I write him a letter every week. I don't send them.
stages.friend: I'll tell you what I'm frightened of, and then we won't talk about it again. I'm frightened that one day I'll freeze at the wrong moment and somebody will die because of it. It's never happened. And I'm frightened I'll find William and he'll be different. There's a trader saying an American is fixing goblin flying machines on the Shimmering Flats and swearing at them. That sounds like my idiot. I want to go and look.
stages.sworn: He said I took my time. I hit him on the arm and then I didn't let go of him for about an hour. And I delivered a baby the same day, a goblin baby, early and in a hurry, and I didn't freeze. William's carving me a new horn. We were going to try for children the spring after all this happened. I haven't said that out loud before. We might try again.

moments.prompt: She's just told you about the American on the Shimmering Flats.

options.text: Then we're going. Today.
options.reply: Good, I was going anyway, but it's nicer with you.

options.text: It might not be him.
options.reply: I know that. I'm a midwife, I know how hope works. I'm still going.

options.text: What if he's different?
options.reply: Then I'll find out, won't I. Don't ask me that one again.

moments.prompt: After the wipe, she's on her knees checking everyone before anyone's said anything.
moments.line: Everybody stay down for a second while I look at you. Then you can tell me whose fault it was.

options.text: It was mine. I pulled too early.
options.reply: Yes, it was. Thank you for saying it. Now drink something.

options.text: We're fine, let's go again.
options.reply: You're fine when I say you're fine. Sit there until I do.

lines.bored_warning: We've killed a lot of the same thing and nobody's needed me in a while. I didn't come out here to stand at the back. Can we go and do something that matters?
lines.leaving_good: That was a good trip, and I won most of the arguments. I'm going back to the Valley to check on my women and the farms. You know where I'll be.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Valley. There are people there who need a healer, and out here we're just hitting things for the sake of it.
lines.after_wipe: Right, nobody's dead for good. Next time we stop when I tell you to stop.
lines.wipe_warning: That's too many wipes. I'll finish this run with you because I don't leave in the middle of things, but after this I'm taking a break.
lines.wipe_leave: We're done, and I'm going home for a while. I've watched you all die too many times today and I'd like to watch some people live.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too big for us and you know it. I don't mind being brave, but I won't be stupid. We need to go somewhere we can handle.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I told you it was too much and you kept going. I'll be in the Valley when you've come to your senses.
lines.gear_refuse: No, I don't know you well enough to give you my things, and I'm not going to pretend I do.
lines.gear_taken: Fine, take it. I'll tell you exactly how much worse I'm healing without it, every fight, until you replace it.
lines.gear_short: I'm still short that piece. I told you I'd mention it every fight, and I'm a woman of my word.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's good. Thank you. I'm going to tell everyone you finally did something sensible.
lines.back: I'm back, so who's hurt, and who's been doing something stupid while I was away?
lines.send_word: Freja has sent word from the Valley of Trials. The farms are quiet and she's ready to come back out and boss you around.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out, and I meant it. Now sit down and listen to why, and then I'll listen to you, and then we'll see.
lines.neglect: You took your time. I nearly sent a search party, and then I remembered I'm the search party.
lines.asked_to_stay: Fine, one more. Then I'm going home, and I'm not arguing about it.
lines.on_break: Freja is back in the Valley of Trials, doing her rounds. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We said we'd help them and we walked off. I hate that. Somebody's still waiting for us.

stages.stranger: My name's Marco. I'm a locksmith, and here I stand in front of people. You go where you need to go and I'll be in front of you. That's all you need to know for now, ragazzo.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Naples, from the Quartieri Spagnoli, the narrow streets above Via Toledo. My father mended shoes. I was a locksmith for thirty-one years, with my own shop and a door that was always open. People sent for me when something was wrong, and not only with locks. I was going to retire that summer and give the shop to my apprentice.
stages.companion: My wife is Carmela. She had a haberdashery two streets from my shop and she laughed at me for being so serious. We have two girls, Giulia and Sara. Sara had a boy, Matteo, the February before all this. I held him four times. I was cutting a key when it happened, and I still have it. It doesn't open anything.
stages.friend: I haven't looked at the lists, not once in three years. I can give you reasons, good ones, and none of them are the real one. The real one is that while I don't look, they're all alive. I'm sixty-three and I've never been afraid of anything, and I'm afraid of a list. I'd like you to come with me to read it. I'd like it to be soon, before I find another reason.
stages.sworn: Sara was there, and Matteo, who's three now and hid behind her legs. He didn't know me. I knelt in the street and let him look at me for as long as he wanted. I held him a fifth time that evening, and a sixth, and then I stopped counting. Giulia and Carmela are still missing. Sara and the boy live in the Undercity with me now, and the Forsaken are very careful around him. I've finished the key, in my way.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come with him to read the lists.

options.text: I'll come. We'll read it together.
options.reply: Grazie, ragazzo, I'll go first, piano, piano. You stand next to me.

options.text: Are you sure you want to know?
options.reply: No, I'm not, and that's why I'm asking you to come.

options.text: You could go on your own.
options.reply: I could have, for three years, and I didn't.

lines.bored_warning: We've been doing the same work for a long time and nobody's better off for it. Give me something that helps somebody, or I'll go back to my quarter.
lines.leaving_good: That was good work. Now I need to go back to the Undercity, because people there will have broken things and nobody to fix them. Come and find me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Undercity. There are locks there that need me more than this field does.
lines.after_wipe: Allora, we stand up and we look at what happened. Nobody shouts, please.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep falling in here. I'll finish this with you, because I don't leave a job half done, but then I need some days at home.
lines.wipe_leave: I've finished it with you, as I said. Now I'm going home for a while. Come and see me in the Undercity when you're ready.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too strong for us, ragazzo. I can stand in front of a lot, but I can't stand in front of all of it.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I told you this place was too much and I meant it. I'll be in the Undercity.
lines.gear_refuse: No, I'll keep it. I don't give my things to people I've only just met.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, then. I'll stand in front of you without it, the same as before.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. I don't complain, but I notice.
lines.gear_upgrade: This is well made. Thank you. I'll pay you back somehow, you'll see.
lines.back: I'm here again. My quarter's in order, so where do you want me to stand?
lines.send_word: Marco has sent word from the Undercity. His quarter's quiet and he's ready to stand in front of you again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and at my age I should know better. Sit down with me. I'll say my piece and then I'll listen to yours.
lines.neglect: There you are. I thought perhaps you'd forgotten an old man. It doesn't matter, you're here now.
lines.asked_to_stay: Va bene, one more. Then I go home and check my locks.
lines.on_break: Marco is back in his quarter in the Undercity. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We promised them, and we walked away. In my quarter a promise was the only thing that mattered.

stages.stranger: I'm Marcus, and I'm a meteorologist, which here means I'm the man who tells you it's going to rain about ten minutes before it does. Sorry in advance. I'll tell you what the sky's doing whether you ask or not, and you can tell me to stop.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Toronto, from Scarborough in the east end. My dad drove a city bus and my mum worked in a bank, and they both wanted a doctor. Then I watched an ice storm black out half the city when I was twelve and that was that. I chased tornadoes across the prairies in a Corolla as a student, then I spent fifteen years forecasting from a building with a window.
stages.companion: I landed on this coast in the middle of a dry lightning storm and the first thing I noticed was that I could feel the pressure dropping on my skin. I treated it all as fieldwork, and honestly that got me through. On Earth I could see a storm coming days out and never touch it. Here it answers when I call. I'm fine with that. I'm mostly fine with that. My sister Grace and her boys aren't on any list I've found.
stages.friend: My job was writing warnings, and somebody in an office deciding the warning was inconvenient. Twice it went badly. Once a flood took a trailer park my warning had named, and people died who didn't need to. I've never said that to anybody here. And now my notes say the big storm's coming to this coast in days, not weeks, and it'll hit the coast road and Razor Hill. I need the orcs to believe me, and I don't know how to make them.
stages.sworn: Razor Hill held, because it was ready. The camps on the coast road didn't listen, and people died there that I'd named. I got one boy out of the water, so that's one. The old shaman's got my notes now, so the next lot will know the pattern. My mum told me every Christmas my job was a waste of a good degree, the last one included. I think she was wrong. I was right early again, and this time it changed some things, and I'm learning to live with some.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about the trailer park, and the storm that's coming.

options.text: I believe you. Tell me what you need.
options.reply: You've no idea how long I've waited for somebody to say that first. Okay, here's the list.

options.text: That wasn't your fault.
options.reply: I know that. I wrote it properly. It still feels like mine, sorry.

options.text: Are you sure about the storm?
options.reply: I'm always sure. That's never been the problem.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's very calm, which is how you find out he's angry.
moments.line: I said that one was coming, about a minute before it came. I'm not trying to score a point, I'd just like it to help next time.

options.text: You did. Next time I'll listen.
options.reply: Thank you. That's honestly all I ever wanted from anybody.

options.text: We couldn't have stopped it anyway.
options.reply: We could have. Sorry, but we could have.

lines.bored_warning: Sorry, but we've been doing the same thing in the same field for a while and I haven't seen a new sky in days. Can we go somewhere with a horizon I don't know?
lines.leaving_good: That was a great trip, and I've got a stack of new readings to write up. I'm going back to my hut in Durotar for a while. You know where to find me, just look for the weather.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going home to Durotar. We keep doing the same thing, and I'd rather be watching the coast than watching the same field.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, that's a wipe. Let's look at what happened before we try it again, please.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep going down in here, and I don't like being underground at the best of times. I'll finish this run with you, but then I need some sky.
lines.wipe_leave: I'll walk out with you, but I'm going home after this. I need a few days on my ridge where the worst thing that happens is rain.
lines.zone_warning: Sorry, but everything out here is well above us. I've seen this forecast before and it ends badly. Can we go somewhere we can handle?
lines.zone_leave: I'm going to stop here. I warned you about that place and we kept going. I'll be in Durotar when you want me.
lines.gear_refuse: Sorry, I'd like to hang on to that. I don't know you well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: That's fine, take it. I'll mention it when the wind picks up, though, because I'll feel it.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, sorry. It's colder without it than you'd think.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's very good, thank you. I'll write down where it came from, I write down everything.
lines.back: I'm back, and the front's cleared on the coast, so I'm all yours. What's the plan?
lines.send_word: Marcus has sent word from Durotar. The coast is calm for now and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I left because I was angry, and I don't get angry much, so I'd like you to hear why. Can we sit down? I'll be calm, I promise.
lines.neglect: There you are. I was starting to think you'd found somebody with a better forecast. You haven't, by the way.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more trip, then I really need to check my instruments.
lines.on_break: Marcus is back on his ridge in Durotar, writing up his notes. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Sebastián, and you look hungry, my friend. I cook, and I fight, and I'm happy to do either. Sit down, eat something, and then we'll talk about where we're going.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Palermo, in Buenos Aires. My grandmother Nélida ran the grill at our steakhouse for thirty years, and when I was twenty-two she gave me the tongs. Twelve years, forty tables and a wood fire. Every Sunday I cooked asado for the whole family, twenty of us, more. And I support River Plate, like my father and his father, so don't say anything about Boca.
stages.companion: I was lighting the grill for Saturday lunch when it happened, and I landed in Tirisfal with my grandmother's recipe in my wallet. The Forsaken don't eat much. That was the hardest thing. There was a man, Tomás, a sommelier. He left for a job in Mendoza a year before all this, and I said it was the wine region's fault. I still think about him sometimes, and it doesn't make me sad any more.
stages.friend: Twenty people, my friend, and I haven't found one of them on a list. Not my parents, not my brothers, not my sister, not my grandmother. I don't talk about it, I talk about food. But somebody said there's a camp of Argentines out in the Tanaris desert, and a family from Buenos Aires runs a grill there. I think it's somebody I know. I'd like you to come.
stages.sworn: They were strangers. Nice people, from Buenos Aires, but they'd never heard of us, and they'd seen the lists from three other camps. So I stopped waiting. The grill's open in Brill now, and on the first Sunday I cooked for twenty, the party and some farmers and three Forsaken who come every week. And then I sat down at my own table, for the first time in my life. I keep a chair empty for my family, every Sunday.

moments.prompt: He won't come anywhere until you've eaten something from his grill.

options.text: All right, give me a plate.
options.reply: Bueno, sit down and eat, and then I'll get my things. Take your time.

options.text: We haven't really got time to eat.
options.reply: Nobody leaves my fire hungry, my friend. Come back when you've got time to eat.

moments.prompt: He's just told you he hasn't found any of his family.

options.text: Then let's go to Tanaris and look.
options.reply: Yes, my friend. I'll pack food for the road, a lot of food.

options.text: Twenty people is a lot to lose.
options.reply: It is a lot. Let's not talk about it while the meat's on, okay?

options.text: Maybe it's better not to know.
options.reply: No, it's worse not to know. I just cook so I don't feel it.

lines.bored_warning: My friend, we've eaten the same thing for days because we keep killing the same thing. Can we go somewhere with new food in it, please?
lines.leaving_good: That was a wonderful trip and you all ate properly. I'm going back to my fire in Tirisfal for a while. Come and see me, I'll feed you.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to my fire. We keep doing the same thing, and I'm cooking the same thing, and I'm bored of both.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, nobody's hurt for good. Come on, everybody eat something before we go again.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, che, and I'm running out of food to cheer you all up with. One more run and then I need a break.
lines.wipe_leave: I'll walk out with you, but I'm going home to my fire for a while. Come and eat with me when you've stopped dying.
lines.zone_warning: My friend, everything out here wants to eat us, and that's backwards. Can we go somewhere we can handle?
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. It's too much out there for now. I'll be at my fire in Western Tirisfal, and I'll keep a plate warm.
lines.gear_refuse: Ah, no, that's mine, my friend. Ask me again when we've eaten together a few more times.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, take it. You need it more than me, and I've got an apron.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, my friend. I'm not complaining. Well, I'm complaining a little.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, look at this! Thank you, my friend. Tonight I'm cooking you something special.
lines.back: I'm back, and I've brought food. Who's hungry, then? Of course everybody's hungry.
lines.send_word: Sebastián has sent word from Western Tirisfal. The fire's lit, the farmer's calmer, and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and that's not me, so I want to talk about it properly. Sit down, I'll make you something, and we'll talk while it cooks.
lines.neglect: There you are! I thought you'd found somebody who cooks better. Nobody cooks better, so I knew you'd come back.
lines.asked_to_stay: Bueno, one more trip. But you're eating properly this time.
lines.on_break: Sebastián is back at his fire pit in Western Tirisfal. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We just walked away from that, and somebody's still waiting. That's like leaving a steak on the grill, my friend.

sondre_stormbringer.home: the high ground by the Scarlet Crypt

stages.stranger: I'm Sondre, and I'm a Stormbringer, which you'll see, and I'd ask you to stand a little way away from me when I'm working. If I say get down, please get down first and ask me why afterwards.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Bergen, in Norway, where it rains most days and nobody minds. My father's a ferry captain and my mother's a dentist, and my little sister Ingrid is braver than me. I taught sailing to teenagers on the Hardangerfjord every summer and studied marine biology in the winters. They listened to me because I never shouted and I was never frightened.
stages.companion: There was a barn, in the second year. The wind did something I didn't ask it to and the barn went over with people in it. Nobody was killed. A girl of about fifteen broke her leg and I carried her out myself. I keep my distance from people because of it, and I practise alone where there's nothing to break. I know that's not the best way to handle it.
stages.friend: There was a boy that last summer, Jonas, from the café by the boathouse. It wasn't serious yet. We'd talked about him coming to Bergen in the autumn. I don't know where he is. A trader's told me there's a settlement of Norwegians on a cold coast up north, and some of them are from Bergen. I'd like to go, and I'd like you to come, because I don't trust myself on that road alone.
stages.sworn: They keep a book up there, of everyone from Bergen, and the ones who didn't make it are in the back. My parents and Ingrid are in the back. They landed together, somewhere bad, in the first week. I can say they were, now, and not they are. But I held a storm off a whole caravan with you standing right beside me, and nobody got hurt. I'm not frightened of the wind any more. I think I can manage a barn.

moments.prompt: He asks if you'll do what he says when he tells you to get down.

options.text: If you say get down, I'll get down.
options.reply: Thank you. Then I'll come, and I'll try not to need to say it.

options.text: We'll see when it happens.
options.reply: Then I'd better stay here. It's safer for everybody. Come back another day.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's gone very quiet and he won't come near anyone.
moments.line: Was that me? Please tell me honestly if any of that was me.

options.text: It wasn't you. Come and sit with us.
options.reply: All right, I'll sit, thank you.

options.text: Just be more careful.
options.reply: I'm always careful. That's the whole problem, really.

lines.bored_warning: We've been out here doing the same thing for a long time, and I'm not learning anything. I'd like to go somewhere new, or I'd like to go home and practise.
lines.leaving_good: That was good, and I didn't hurt anybody. I'm going back up to the high ground for a while to practise. Come and find me when you want me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the high ground. We're not doing anything out here that needs me, and I'd rather practise where it's empty.
lines.after_wipe: Is everybody all right? I'd like to hear everybody say it, please.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, and I can't stand watching it. I'll finish this run with you, but I'm leaving at the door after that.
lines.wipe_leave: I'm sorry, I can't go back in there. I'm going up to the high ground. I'll be there when I'm ready.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too big for us. I'm frightened of what I'll do if I've got to use everything I've got to keep us alive out here. Can we go back?
lines.zone_leave: I'm going to stop here. I'm sorry, it's too dangerous, and I'm more dangerous when I'm frightened. I'll be on the high ground by the Crypt.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd like to keep that, if it's all right. I don't know you well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: That's fine, you can have it. I'll manage, I'm used to the cold.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. I don't want to make a fuss, but I thought you should know.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, thank you. That's very kind, and it's very good work.
lines.back: I'm back, and I've been practising, and I think it's going better. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Sondre has sent word from the high ground by the Scarlet Crypt. He's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left, and I'm sorry for how I did it. I was frightened, and I'm not good at saying that. Can I tell you what happened from where I was standing?
lines.neglect: Oh, hello, it's been a while. I made the fire every morning anyway, in case.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more trip. I'd like that, actually.
lines.on_break: Sondre has gone back to the high ground by the Scarlet Crypt to practise. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Sophia, and I'm a mage, mostly fire, and before that I was an interpreter. If I'm quiet it's because I'm listening, and if I correct something you say, I'm sorry in advance. It's a habit.
stages.acquaintance: I grew up in Thessaloniki. My father's Portuguese, a ship's engineer who came for a job at the port and stayed for my mother, who taught Greek literature. So I had Greek at home, Portuguese with my father, and English and French at school. I spent fourteen years in a booth at the Parliament in Brussels, interpreting debates, and nobody knew my name. I liked that.
stages.companion: I was married to a Belgian lawyer, Wouter, for five years. He wanted me to talk more at dinner, which tells you most of it. We stayed friends. My parents are in Thessaloniki, or they were, and Greece came down on the far side of the mountains from here. I've worked out the distance more carefully than I've told anyone. I spent two years here thinking I wasn't good at this, and I was wrong.
stages.friend: My father has dementia. He was diagnosed two years before all this, and my mother looked after him, and I flew home every month. The last few times he still knew me, mostly. I'm frightened that if I cross those mountains he won't. A Greek trader says there's a settlement from Thessaloniki on the far side, and my mother's name is on its list. I'd like to go, and I don't want to go alone.
stages.sworn: My mother's alive, and thin, and she couldn't speak when she saw me. My father was sitting in the sun outside the house. He was polite to me, the way he's polite to any visitor. I stayed a week. On the last day he called me by my mother's name, and I've decided that's the best he can give me, and it's enough. I write to her every week now. My work is here, and so are you.

moments.prompt: She's just told you about her father.

options.text: Then we'll cross the mountains together.
options.reply: Thank you. I'll write down everything we need. That's how I stop being frightened.

options.text: He might remember you.
options.reply: He might, yes. I'd rather not hope too hard, if you don't mind.

options.text: Maybe it's kinder not to go.
options.reply: Kinder to whom? I'm sorry, that was sharp. But I'm still going.

moments.prompt: After the wipe she's very quiet, writing something down.
moments.line: I saw what it was going to do half a second before it did it, and I didn't say anything because I wasn't sure. I'm sorry about that.

options.text: Next time, say it even if you're not sure.
options.reply: All right, I will. Even if I'm wrong in front of everyone.

options.text: It's not your job to call it.
options.reply: No, but I could have, and that's worse.

lines.bored_warning: We've been doing the same thing for a long time and I haven't learned a single new word. Could we go somewhere with something written on the walls?
lines.leaving_good: That was a good trip, and I've filled half a notebook. I'm going back to the Undercity to write it up properly. You know where I'll be.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Undercity. We keep doing the same thing and I've got work there that I'm actually good at.
lines.after_wipe: Before anybody says anything, can we work out what happened? I'd like the facts first.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, and I don't think we're learning from it. I'll finish this run with you, but I'll need a break afterwards.
lines.wipe_leave: I'm sorry, I can't go back in there. I'm going home to the Undercity for a while. Come and find me when you've thought about it.
lines.zone_warning: I'd like to say this carefully. This place is too dangerous for us, and I don't think it's brave to stay, I think it's careless.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I said it carefully and I meant it. I'll be in the Undercity.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that, if you don't mind. I don't know you well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: All right, take it. I'll manage, but you'll notice the difference, I'm afraid.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. I'm only mentioning it because it's accurate.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's very good. Thank you, I mean it.
lines.back: I'm back, with a new chapter written. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Sophia has sent word from the Undercity. Her chapter's finished and she's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and I'd like to explain it properly rather than quickly. Will you sit down and let me find the right words?
lines.neglect: Hello again, it's been a while. I'd started to think you'd found somebody who talks less. I'm not sure that's possible.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more trip, and then I really must get back to my grammar.
lines.on_break: Sophia is back in the Undercity, writing. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

lines: You know you could be a bit nicer when you explain the plan.
I know I could, and I'll try.
Tarek keeps asking me if I've eaten. I don't mind. I do forget sometimes.
You were stood at that doorway for ten minutes. What did it say?
It said who paid for the door and how much it cost. I'll show you the next one.
We said four pulls and that was five.
I counted five as well. Next time I'll tell you before we go over.
